Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 23.10.2019 passed in MVC No.117/2019 by the I Additional Small Causes Judge & MACT (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioners therein have preferred this appeal.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
That on 02.12.2018 at about 5.00 p.m. when one Ram Kumar was riding his motor cycle on 80 feet road and when he reached near Brigade Omega Apartment,
Kumaraswamy Layout, Bangalore, a car bearing registration No.KA-05-MQ-425 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against his motor bike, because of which, the said - Ram Kumar expired.
The petitioners are said to be the dependants of the deceased and preferred MVC No.117/2019.

4. The Tribunal, based on the evidence let in, has awarded a compensation of Rs.14,14,300/- along with interest @ 9 % p.a. under the following heads:-
1 For loss of Estate Rs. 15,000-00 2 For funeral Expenses Rs. 15,000-00 For conveyance expenses 3 Rs. 23,500-00 and Medical expenses 4

sentences.text: 5. Not satisfied by the same, the petitioners have preferred this appeal.
6. Admittedly, the accident happened in the year 2018.
The age of the deceased at the time of the accident was 22 years and was a Bachelor.
The petitioners have not established the income of the deceased before the Tribunal.
Hence, as per the Lok Adalath chart, the income of the deceased is notionally fixed at Rs.12,500/- per month.
Given the age of the deceased, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma & Ors vs Delhi Transport Corp.& Anr [2009(6) SCC 121], multiplier of '18' is applicable.

sentences.text: As per the law down by the Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% needs to be added to his income as future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 50% of income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal expenses as he was a bachelor.
Thus, on the count of 'loss of dependency', petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.18,90,000/- (12,500 + 40% x 12 x 18 x 1/2 ).
Further, petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards 'loss of estate and funeral expenses'.

Further,
each of the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- and together they are entitled to a sum of Rs.80,000/- (40,000x2=80,000) towards 'loss of consortium'.
Further, based on the actual bills submitted by the petitioners, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.23,500/- towards 'medical expenses'.
I deem the same to be appropriate.

7. Thus, the compensation to the petitioners under different heads are modified as hereunder:-
 AMOUNT AMOUNT Sl. HEAD OF AWARDED BY AWARDED BY No. COMPENSATION THE TRIBUNAL THIS COURT  IN RS.
IN RS.

Funeral expenses 15,000-00 -  Conveyance expenses 3 23,500-00 23,500-00  and medical expenses 4 Loss of consortium - 80,000-00 5 Loss of Dependency 13,60,800-00 18,90,000-00  Total 14,14,300-00 20,23,500-00 8.

Thus, the petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.6,09,200/- (Rs.20,23,500/-
minus Rs.14,14,300/-).

Hence, the following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii.

The total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified and petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.6,09,200/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Nine Thousand Two Hundred only) over and above what has been already awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition before the Tribunal till the date of realization.
